Eve: Heads up — after the kernel-chooser tweak we see a clear p95 tail regression on Mistral 8x7B for sliding-window long-context jobs. Repro in perf harness, failing traces attached.
perf-bot: perf-harness run 1768504200 completed: p50=28ms p95=143ms (baseline p95=86ms) on seq=4096 batch=8 sliding_window=true
Sam: Hmm. Did the selector accidentally pick the generic matmul path instead of the rotary-optimized kernel for 8x7B? That would explain tail spikes.
Jordan: Can you paste the kernel selection log and the model config (rope_scale, max_position_embeddings)?
Eve: Log snippet:
```
[2026-06-02T10:45:19Z] kernel_selector: model=mistral-8x7b seq=4096 chosen=matmul_block4 fallback=no reason=rope_mismatch
[2026-06-02T10:45:19Z] kernel_selector: score(matmul_block4)=0.78 score(rotary_fast)=0.74
```
Profiler heatmap (summary):
```
attention_kernel            42.1%
kv_copy_and_shift           18.3%
memset_or_zero_fill         12.6%
softmax_norm                9.4%
other                      17.6%
```
Sam: "rope_mismatch" stands out. Did we remove the hard-coded rope_scale override in the ingest layer last week?
ciaran: Yes — I removed the ingest override that forced rope_scale=1.0 for Mistral variants. The model artifact for 8x7B sometimes expects rope_scale ~0.125 in our older bundles; a mismatch can change attention mask semantics and force extra KV copying.
Sana: Also seeing lots of `memset` churn in the profiler — sliding-window pointer resets cause frequent KV buffer re-writes. If attention mask alignment is wrong we may be zeroing more memory than necessary.
Eve: Repro command I used:
```
./run_perf --model mistral-8x7b --seq 4096 --batch 8 --sliding_window --pprof out.pb
```
Sam: Quick try: force kernel selector to prefer `rotary_fast` and set runtime override `max_position_embeddings=8192`. Does p95 recover?
Jordan: I ran that locally: forcing `rotary_fast` drops p95 back to ~92ms but throughput drops ~6% (likely due to different blocking). So kernel + batching heuristics both matter.
ciaran: My hypothesis: our kernel scoring currently uses avg_seq distribution. For sliding-window workloads the tail-case (longest requested prefix) is more important. We need tail-aware scoring (weight >90th percentile). Also guard for rope_scale mismatch between model metadata and runtime config.
Sana: Agreed. We should also add a small KV coalescing/opportunistic copy pass to reduce pointer resets during sliding window shifts.
Eve: I pushed a branch `perf/mistral-rope-guard` with:
- kernel_selector: tail_weight=3.0 experiment
- a warning when rope_scale != model_meta.rope_scale
- a unit test that simulates rope mismatch kernel path
CI: perf job queued from the branch.
Jordan: Nice. Can we also add a microbenchmark that isolates KV-copy path (step-only loop) to get memset heatmap and GPU mem throughput numbers? If we see OOM or high PCIe traffic we may tune batch size.
Sam: I'll add the microbenchmark and a perf job. Short-term mitigation: set runtime config `kernel_selector.tail_weight=3.0` and re-enable rope_scale override for mistral-8x7b until the fix lands. That brought our p95 back in smoke tests.
perf-bot: CI perf job queued: perf/mistral-rope-guard #452
ciaran: I'll follow up with a PR to change scoring to use q90/q95 quantiles and add the rope guard. @infra-oncall FYI in case the perf jobs spike GPU usage.
Eve: Thanks all. Action items: Sam add KV microbenchmark, Ciaran change scoring + rope guard, Jordan validate throughput vs p95 tradeoff for rotary_fast, Sana prototype KV coalescing. I'll track in the branch and link the perf dashboard once CI finishes. :thumbsup:
